title: Activation credit v2 — anchoring + time-sliced burn rate
content:
Problem: starter credits currently feel noisy and are exploited by batch-y ingestion patterns. Need a V2 that: 1) aligns to expected unit economics per activated developer, 2) reduces free-rider abuse for long-running autogenerated workloads, 3) signals value (low-friction trial) but still nudges to commit.

High-level idea: Anchored activation credits + time-sliced burn rate + cache-aware discounts.
- Anchor: give a headline $X credit sized to cover an expected narrow-window usage that correlates with product value (e.g., first 3 interactive sessions). Anchor size chosen using LTV -> CAC back-of-envelope.
- Time-sliced burn rate: credits have an internal clock that makes subsequent token burns scale up slightly over time within the credit window. Think: first 10k tokens burn at 1x, next 40k tokens burn at 1.8x, >50k tokens burn at 3x. Purpose: give friction to huge consumption while preserving exploratory usage.
- Cache-aware discount: tokens served from prefix/KV cache consume credits at 0.2x to reflect lower marginal GPU work. Encourages productive interactive workflows that benefit from caching.

Assumptions (conservative):
- Amortized infra cost per GPU-hour (mixed fleet for hosted small-medium model mix): $3.50 / GPU-hour.
- Effective throughput across mixed models averaged to 20M tokens / GPU-hour (around 5.6 tokens/sec sustained).
- Therefore raw infra cost per token = $3.50 / 20,000,000 = $0.000000175 -> 1.75e-7 $/token.
- Add infra overhead (storage, network, control plane) + ops margin => multiply by 3.5 -> blended unit cost ~ 6.125e-7 $/token (0.0000006125).
- Target gross margin on hosted trial consumption: 70% (we are subsidizing activation), so target price-equivalent for credit budgeting ~ unit cost / (1 - margin) = 6.125e-7 / 0.3 = 2.04e-6 $/token. Use anchor math off this number.

Anchor sizing (two variants):
A) Micro anchor (low-friction): $5 credit. Equivalent token budget at price-equivalent: tokens = 5 / 2.04e-6 ≈ 2.45M tokens.
  - At 20M tokens/GPU-hour, 2.45M tokens ≈ 0.1225 GPU-hours ≈ 7.35 minutes of GPU time.
  - Real-world: around 50-150 interactive prompts depending on length.
B) Focus anchor (higher signal): $20 credit -> ~9.8M tokens -> ~0.49 GPU-hours (~29 min). Better for enterprise or integration trials.

But naive full-coverage at 1x burn makes anchor exploitable by background ingestion. Enter time-sliced burn:
- Design: first 250k tokens at 1.0x, next 2M tokens at 1.8x, remainder at 3.0x. Effective tokens consumed by credit = raw_tokens * multiplier.
- Example micro anchor $5 (nominal raw token budget 2.45M): with slices effective budget shrinks because multipliers increase. Back-of-envelope effective raw tokens allowed before credits exhausted: solve for raw where (min(250k, r)*1.0 + min(2M, max(0,r-250k))*1.8 + max(0, r-2.25M)*3.0) * price_equiv = 5. Numeric approx: first 250k -> cost 250k*2.04e-6=0.51, next 2M -> 2M*1.8*2.04e-6=7.34, already >5 so micro anchor effectively pays for ~ (5-0.51)/(2.04e-6*1.8) ≈ (4.49)/(3.672e-6) ≈ 1.22M tokens in the mid-slab + 250k = ~1.47M raw tokens. Much less than 2.45M naive, which is exactly intended.

Cache-aware discount math: cached_token_multiplier = 0.2x (i.e., 80% discount vs cold tokens). Implementation: credit ledger marks a tag on tokens classified as cache-hit and applies multiplier. This yardsticks to ops cost because cached tokens use modest CPU/RAM and ignore many GPU cycles.

Latency-tier multiplier: low-latency customers (our premium offering) get a multiplier bonus: tokens consumed on low-latency routes burn at 1.4x credit usage relative to standard to reflect reserved capacity cost. Alternatively, reserved customers can opt-out of credit burn entirely (credits used only for payg). Need to gate this by account type.

Activation funnel experiments (A/B):
- Variant A (control): $10 flat credit, flat burn 1x, no cache-awareness.
- Variant B (time-sliced): $10 credit, slices [100k@1x, 900k@1.6x, rest@2.8x], cache discount 0.2x.
- Variant C (anchored + gated): $20 credit but only redeemable over a 30-day window and first 3 unique interactive sessions get 0.5x burn to encourage exploration.
Metrics to track: activation->paid conversion, median tokens consumed in first 7 days, proportion of batch-y long jobs vs interactive sessions, marginal cost of credit usage (on infra), fraud/abuse signals.

Back-of-envelope cohort unit-econ: assume micro anchor ($5) deployed to 10k signups -> gross credit exposure = $50k. Expected redemption rate (realistic) 15% -> $7.5k actual. If 3% convert to paid with ARPU $120/yr -> revenue = 36 * 100? Wait that's wrong, recalc properly: 10k signups -> paid conversions 3% = 300 customers -> ARR per converted = $120 => ARR = $36k/yr. So $7.5k upfront credit cost to get $36k ARR is promising if CAC is low and retention decent. This is rough but shows sizing.

Edge cases & abuse vectors:
- Background ingestion: large sequential batch jobs that replay prompts. Mitigation: sessionization heuristic + rate-limited credit redemption per account per hour (soft cap), detect heavy sequential token flow and route to payg-only lane.
- Sybil signups: throttle credits per payment method or require low-friction phone/email verification after 2 redeems.
- Cache label spoofing: ensure cache-hit classification based on server-side prefix/deduping not client-supplied headers.

Implementation notes for ledger:
- Credits are fungible, but ledger entries track: raw_tokens_charged, effective_credits_debited, reason_tag (cache|latency|slice-index). Use that to rebuild and audit.
- For UI: display an "effective remaining tokens" metric that factors in multipliers so users understand remaining value.
- On redemption UX: show a short explainer: "Your activation credit gives you X minutes of testing; usage beyond early exploration is charged differently to prevent misuse." Keep wording simple.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Fine-tune multipliers empirically vs infra telemetry — where does 1.8x/3x come from? Run small infra trace against top-10 customer prompts to profile token-level GPU work.
- Decide decay window: should slices reset after 30 days? 7 days? We probably want a 30-day window for enterprise but 7 for free-tier to prevent long-term hoarding.
- UX experiments: can we visualize "session-burn heatmap" in console? Data product asks: availability of per-token cache flag and route-level SLO tag.
- Legal: verify we can show dollar-equivalent to users without implying a guaranteed monetary value (check legal phrasing).

Quick action plan (next 2 weeks):
- Spike: implement ledger prototype + simulated burn calculator that given sequence of tokens+cache-hit flags emits credit-debits. (owner: Omar)
- Telemetry: gather 7-day sample of per-token GPU cycles for top-50 routes to justify multipliers. (owner: Leah + infra)
- UX microcopy + experiment config for A/B. (owner: Maya)
- Security: list heuristics to gate sybil abuse and integrate with fraud signals. (owner: Security team)

Bottom line: anchored credits with escalating burn multipliers + cache discounts give us a flexible playground to preserve low-friction trials while protecting unit economics and disincentivizing automated free-runs. Need to test real telemetry to anchor multipliers and tune conversion economics.
